title: Recorded 1.15 million accepted buildings beyond the six states
summary: The November 4 early-morning checkpoint recorded 71 new accepted regions containing 1,147,324 buildings, with 47,953 recorded geometry changes. The completed six-state product remained protected and was counted separately.
note: These are accepted regional outputs, not a completed or newly published nationwide release. Geometry-change counts do not establish accuracy gains.
details: At 03:46 EST, a separate incremental check covered 54 regions and 792,827 buildings; that scope does not cover every latest geometry. Input preparation, I/O and delayed intermediate-file retirement continued to constrain production later that day.

title: Recomputed source-image sensitivity and exact clustered intervals
summary: Recomputed the frozen 171-modified-building results across six source-image groups, including leave-one-image-out checks and all 46,656 ordered cluster resamples. The NAIP-frame mean changes stayed at +2.77 percentage points for IoU and +5.53 for boundary F1 at 1 m.
note: The exact 95% interval was +1.06 to +5.18 points for IoU and -0.73 to +11.08 for F1. Positive leave-one-image-out means did not remove the uncertainty in mean boundary improvement.
details: Original-coordinate results remained negative. The exact enumeration is reported alongside the earlier Monte Carlo interval; it does not add independent images or training data. Matching and exclusion accounting were reconciled while preserving the 2,019 fixed pairs.

title: Prepared decline diagnostics and blinded comparison cases
summary: Identified 47 IoU declines and 54 boundary-F1 declines under the fixed threshold, with 60 buildings in their union. Prepared a 60-case annotated diagnostic book and a 120-case blinded A/B book with controls and a blank review form.
note: The case sample was selected using metric outcomes and is not an unbiased estimate of correctness. No human annotations or causal judgments were invented.
details: Using frozen accepted-operation labels, 41 of the IoU declines and 51 of the F1 declines were addition-only cases. Exact geometric decomposition explains the score arithmetic relative to the reference, but does not decide which observed roof outline is correct.

title: Audited all files in the frozen national publication package
summary: Scanned all 3,522 files in the local immutable October 27 package, containing 150,261,726 records. IDs were nonempty and unique, and manifest file checks passed. The scan found 233 topologically invalid geometries, all inspected as inherited legacy records.
note: This audited the local frozen publication package, not fresh remote bytes or live production. Data integrity is separate from footprint accuracy and validation representativeness.
details: Original geometry and modern modification flags were absent on 124,918,110 legacy records. The remaining 25,343,616 records had original/delivered pairs: 927,559 flagged modified and 24,416,057 flagged unchanged, with no detected WKB/flag contradictions in those paired records. Legacy unknown flags remain unknown. No geometries were repaired during this audit; manuscript totals still require release-version reconciliation.

title: Kept quality checks after testing faster processing variants
summary: Tested processing reductions on real building cohorts. Removing neighborhood/quality checks changed one 468-building cohort from 14 to 367 modifications and produced unacceptable area changes, so that route was rejected.
note: The fastest quality-preserving warm-stage result was about 1.5 times the baseline and missed the preset twofold target. A national end-to-end improvement was not established.
details: Process reuse and header-cache comparisons also had mixed results. Their tested correctness did not by itself justify deployment as production acceleration.

title: Separated saved study areas from fixed analysis records
summary: Published a Data & scope workflow for saving named boundaries and explicitly loading fixed original-data worksets. Statistics, charts, processing, LoD1 and data exports now choose all workset records, the exact selection, or records intersecting a saved study area.
status: Workflow published and verified on public data
note: Map movement and styling do not silently change analytical inputs. Empty selections stay empty, and selecting a smaller subset does not erase partial-source status.
details: Saved areas and record provenance survive projects. Map composition records a visual frame separately from data-export scope. The browser loading budgets remain explicit.

title: Published an interaction prototype for a local computation engine
summary: Published a standalone prototype covering pairing, managed runtimes, optional inspection of existing environments, custom-runtime checks and separate input/output storage choices. Its simulated states can be explored in English and Chinese, including on a phone.
note: This release is a simulated interface prototype. No native installer or working local computation engine was released or enabled.
details: The prototype labels its simulated device state and makes no real engine or third-party-service requests. It preserves user results and external software in the proposed uninstall flow.

title: Added named local projects and a blank workspace
summary: Added browser-local projects, project export/import and a blank-workspace action. Cache controls release fetched neighborhoods and research-model caches while keeping current work and saved projects.
note: Projects use browser storage and portable .usbf.json files. Cloud synchronization is not part of this release.
details: Project restoration was checked alongside the existing data, language and model workflows.

title: Published the national USBF PMTiles display archive
summary: Published a 33.96 GB PMTiles display archive derived from the frozen 150,261,726-record publication and connected it to the default map. Public checks covered DC, New York, Los Angeles and Boston; the full public archive checksum matched.
note: Display tiles may be clipped or simplified. Complete original polygons remain in GeoParquet and load for explicit data operations; the underlying mixed-version inventory was not regenerated by this display release.
details: Map navigation uses tiled display caching instead of repeatedly reading the original GeoParquet. The display manifest records the source release and immutable archive version.

title: Added an independent OpenStreetMap building layer
summary: Connected an OpenFreeMap OpenStreetMap building layer separately from the VIDA source subset. Public-browser checks rendered real upstream tiles in DC, New York and Los Angeles and checked project restoration and mobile layout.
note: This is a display layer. Its tile attributes do not establish measured building heights or complete original analytical geometry.

title: Checked complete bounded reads from comparison providers
summary: Added matching-ID enumeration for DC, stable pagination for NYC, and all matching row-group reads for GBA within explicit limits. Progressive loading, cancellation, retry and cache coverage are shown to the user.
status: Provider reads checked on real data
note: A completed bounded request does not imply complete provider coverage beyond its area or limits.
details: For the tested DC bounds, a count-only endpoint reported 15,279 while both ID enumeration and independently paginated records returned 15,277. Acceptance therefore checked the actual matching ID set.

title: Made original analysis layers and attribute-table scope explicit
summary: Added layer-purpose labels and an explicit original-data loading action. USBF original records become a separate fixed analysis layer with their source geometry, attributes and provenance. Its attribute table can show all loaded records, including hidden or offscreen rows.
note: Tile previews retain their display scope. Loading a bounded original-data layer does not turn the full remote source into a local analytical dataset.
details: Original layers keep their loading area, partial status and licenses through project restoration. Cancellation cannot add a late result.

title: Added range selection and vector processing workflows
summary: Published shared range controls for map views, Census state/county boundaries, boxes, polygons and loaded masks. Added original-record selection, selected exports, extraction, clipping, erase, merge, dissolve and related vector operations.
note: Browser record, vertex and read budgets still apply. Selecting a large administrative boundary can produce an explicitly partial result.
details: Results become new layers with input scope and lineage. Selection and processing use original source records, while map tiles remain the display path.

title: Tested and deployed batched retirement of verified inputs
summary: A matched 24-frame comparison checked identical input arrays, masks and probabilities while batching verified loose-file retirement. The measured retirement step was about 3.54 times faster; the combined copy/seal/route/retire segment was about 1.40 times faster.
note: These are matched stage measurements, not national production speedups. The first production use also checked 64 real frames before broader use of that bounded route.

title: Verified completion of a large archival cleanup campaign
summary: The completed campaign retired 786,281 eligible source files and 224,333 directories after archival and restoration checks: 1,010,614 source namespace entries in total.
note: This is a verified source-retirement count, not the net decrease in the filesystem quota counter. Other production writes and later cleanup campaigns are counted separately.
details: Current source data, protected products and assets still needed by active consumers remained outside the retirement scope.

title: Prepared a tracked revision and manuscript response sheet
summary: Prepared a reviewable manuscript revision and a comment-by-comment response sheet. The revision retained the 23 original comments and identified unresolved evidence checks concerning validation scope, reference frames and data integrity.
note: The response and tracked suggestions were delivered as review materials. The outstanding scientific questions motivated the supplementary diagnostics completed on November 4.
details: The revision preserves the source manuscript and documents proposed wording separately from the remaining validation questions.

title: Recovered execution after file-count backpressure
summary: File-count guards paused scientific processing even though bytes remained available. Verified archival and restoration of eligible older inputs created room to resume processing, while automated cleanup continued.
status: Execution resumed; capacity remained a constraint
note: Resuming tasks did not immediately increase accepted building counts. Retirement totals describe eligible source files removed after verification, not the net change in a live filesystem.
details: The work exposed a dependency cycle: completing regions required more inputs, while some cleanup waited for those regions to finish. Older eligible inputs provided a separate recovery route.

title: Stopped reloading covered building views on every zoom
summary: Added a bounded decoded-neighborhood cache and reused prepared map sources for covered views. In four repeated DC zooms, the local comparison changed from roughly 6.3–6.9 seconds with 11 GeoParquet requests each to 10–106 milliseconds with no additional GeoParquet reads.
note: This comparison concerns one already covered neighborhood. It is not a cold-load or nationwide latency guarantee.
details: In-flight covered requests and existing geometry survive zoom changes. Publication changes invalidate cached source data.

title: Added Chinese controls and repaired model visibility
summary: Published an English/Chinese interface option and repaired the Models visibility control. Local and public-browser checks covered language switching, model controls and phone layout.
note: Dataset names, raw attribute names, formats and source values retain their meaning when the interface language changes.

title: Recorded accepted output from the revised regional route
summary: The dated production checkpoint recorded 200,071 accepted buildings in new regions, including 51,818 added that day. The completed six-state product remained at 25,092,517 buildings.
note: The revised regional counter and the earlier hollow-only counter describe different processing cohorts. Neither is a count of a completed new nationwide release.
details: Rolling scheduling and input recovery continued, with input preparation and I/O still limiting progress.

title: Revised the regional route and input-reuse plan
summary: A revised 2,422-building prototype produced 52 geometry changes. Work also moved toward indexed bundles of imagery, elevation, masks and model probabilities so later refinement could reuse the expensive front end.
note: The 52 changes are processing outcomes, not verified accuracy gains. Earlier stand-alone fast regions had sometimes retired their sensor inputs, so complete reuse could not be assumed.
details: The retained input bundle must contain actual raster arrays and provenance, not only JSON execution records. Regional limits and restore checks are needed before retiring loose inputs.

title: Compared the hollow-only route with full refinement
summary: Compared the two routes on 29 matched regions containing 250,395 buildings. The hollow-only route changed no buildings in that cohort, while full refinement changed 7,467. Median CPU processing time per region was 34 seconds and 704 seconds, respectively.
note: The faster route covered far fewer editing operations. These timings exclude input acquisition, inference and queueing; they are not national end-to-end speedups.
details: The comparison motivated a revised first pass that retained useful local changes, rather than using footprint coverage alone as the success measure.

title: Connected US Buildings directly to the live USBF publication
summary: Made USBF the default building layer and connected bounded GeoParquet reads to the public manifest. The viewer checks for publication changes on opening, periodically in a visible tab, and through a manual update action.
note: The checked October 27 publication snapshot contained 150,261,726 records in 3,522 tiles, combining updated six-state data with existing records elsewhere. Those totals are not a count of completed new refinement.
details: Source heights remain inherited heights; missing input nDSM and missing building height are different states. Unknown edit flags remain distinct from false. The viewer loads neighborhoods rather than processing the national inventory in the browser.

title: Published US Buildings 1.3 with analysis and project tools
summary: Published local and URL imports, GeoParquet and raster support, scoped statistics, charts, spatial tools, coordinate conversion, drawing, project save/restore, and map/data downloads. Added local OBJ/GLB placement and LoD1 generation while retaining the experimental roof-model collection.
note: Statistics use explicit loaded-data snapshots. PMTiles display fragments are not treated as complete source geometry, and export limits and truncation are recorded.
details: The final validation record includes 748 semantic checks, 54 browser checks and six real USBF city probes. A public browser test downloaded 166 DC records from its loaded view and checked their height statistics and identifiers; this was a scoped data-access check, not a nationwide analysis.

title: Updated the personal research pages, CV and resume
summary: Updated the personal website with USBF data and code links, the US Buildings workspace and current roof-reconstruction experiments. Added the 2026 hydrogen-logistics paper to the CV and one-page resume and updated the contact information.
note: The paper was already published; this date records the website and document update.

title: Expanded the building-data comparison catalog
summary: Connected GBA US footprints and supplied heights, Microsoft legacy tiles, Overture and official DC/NYC sources. Added source-specific VIDA subsets and download links for other inventories.
note: The sources differ in date, coverage and provenance. They are comparison layers, not independent accuracy references; download-only resources are identified separately.

title: Tested a separate hollow-only fast pass
summary: Tested a route that only proposes strictly supported interior holes in large source footprints while retaining their outer boundaries. A 5,046-building warm-input comparison produced byte-identical outputs after batching changes; its production stage changed from 692.31 to 33.86 seconds.
note: Both compared outputs contained zero accepted hole changes. This is a stage timing, not national end-to-end throughput or evidence of improved geometry accuracy.
details: A separate Chicago chain prepared 59 real frames, ran frozen-model inference and generated 15,825 footprints, also with no accepted hole changes. The route is a distinct method version, not a silent replacement for full V7. Shared fast/full-stage input reuse remained follow-up work.

title: Released and tested the public USBF workflow
summary: Published USBF_src v0.1.2 with downloadable example inputs and frozen checkpoints. A public run passed 21 software tests, real model inference, three-building generation, fixed-geometry evaluation of 2,019 pairs, and notebook Run All.
note: This verifies small-example generation and evaluation replay. It does not reconstruct the full paper from all historical imagery or rerun the original training.
details: Original code uses MIT and model checkpoints use CC BY 4.0; input data retain their component terms. The later v0.1.3 title/citation update does not represent a new computational experiment.

title: Compared point, optical-fusion and neighborhood models
summary: Compared 18 models across six configurations and three seeds, including a linear baseline, point MLP, optical fusion, local context and reliability gating. Ran target inference on 120 buildings and eight reconstruction strategies on 24 buildings.
note: Optical and neighborhood features improved tree-point rejection in parts of the source evaluation, but the gate showed no supported advantage over the matched context-fusion baseline. Independent US roof ground truth is still absent.

sources.label: LoD2 models, results and point-cloud viewer

details: The comparison reports roof-point retention alongside rejected tree points. Native roof output and a passing shell check establish execution and topology diagnostics, not improved roof accuracy.

title: Rechecked roof retention on spatially separated source areas
summary: Trained 48 additional models across four spatial folds, four model families and three seeds. The recheck used separated training, calibration and evaluation areas to test whether the calibrated roof-retention target transferred within the source scene.
note: The lowest evaluation roof retention was 97.37%, despite a 99.5% calibration target. These folds reuse a previously studied scene; they are not independent cities or a new blind geographic test.

sources.label: LoD2 models, results and point-cloud viewer

details: Together with the first 18 models, this round contains 66 trained models. The results motivate better validation of observation reliability and roof preservation before treating a more elaborate gate as an improvement.

title: Added experimental roof models and data exports to US Buildings
summary: Added browsing for eight US experimental buildings under three methods and 20 Dutch 3DBAG training-reference roofs. Connected model inspection with the footprint/height view and added model downloads, shareable views and mobile access.
note: US experiments and Dutch training references remain separate collections. Displaying a model does not provide independent validation of its roof geometry.

sources.label: LoD2 models, results and point-cloud viewer

title: Replayed the OSM confirmation rule on nine circle candidates
summary: Replayed the September 18 confirmation rule on the historical circle candidates. All nine returned to the original GBA geometry; the primary sample retained 2,019 fixed pairs, with 171 modified buildings and 1,848 unchanged buildings.
note: The candidates lacked eligible exact-reference confirmation. This did not test the shape threshold on a set of confirmed circle replacements.
details: The remaining local-change geometries stayed fixed. Both original-reference and NAIP-frame evaluations were retained; the reference-frame sensitivity remains part of the interpretation.

title: Checked circular and elliptical reference targets separately
summary: Screened 96 complete near-circular or elliptical SpaceNet targets and found nine unique GBA matches. Processed those nine plus four fixed unmatched targets. The final confirmation policy retained GBA geometry for all nine matched cases.
note: There was no successful rectangle-to-circle correction in this sample. The nine raw-coordinate pairs, seven registered pairs and four unmatched targets remain separate from the primary 2,019-pair sample.
details: Six matched cases had rectilinear GBA outlines against near-circular references; three already had curved GBA outlines. The six disagreements were already unchanged before the confirmation gate. Unmatched targets retain NA scores rather than zeros.

title: Measured the extent of changes in the historical regional cohort
summary: Recomputed geometry differences for 48,772 buildings from the historical regional experiment. Its 1,887 modified buildings contained 71,194.68 m² of additions and 21,071.32 m² of removals, for 92,266.00 m² of symmetric difference.
note: This is the older regional research version, not the current six-state production cohort. Geometry differences measure what changed, not whether it became more accurate.
details: Net area change was +50,123.36 m². The audit kept the original operation groups and checked all geometry pairs; these area totals are not extrapolated to the national inventory.

title: Ran a minimal USBF example in a clean CPU environment
summary: Packaged real inputs and the frozen B0/B1 models into a local workflow. Generated three example buildings, checked their final geometry against the historical outputs, recomputed the 2,019 fixed geometry pairs, and ran the notebook from a fresh kernel.
note: At this stage public download and remote execution still required verification. Complete 32-frame generation and historical retraining were not executed.
details: The examples include a changed outline, an unchanged building and a circle candidate that falls back to GBA without confirmation. Evaluation rasterizes the frozen geometries instead of using stored score CSVs as its input.

title: Compared footprint changes in a common NAIP reference frame
summary: Analyzed 171 addition/removal cases within 2,019 fixed GBA–SpaceNet pairs. With the reference moved into the NAIP image frame and both footprint products held fixed, mean IoU for these modified cases changed from 69.74% to 72.51%; boundary F1 at 1 m changed from 54.41% to 59.93%.
note: Raw-coordinate results were negative. These are reference-agreement results in Las Vegas, not nationwide accuracy estimates or a test of absolute positioning.
details: The reference shift used non-building image features; products and fixed matches were not fitted to the scoring polygons. The modified groups contain 144 additions only, 20 removals only and seven combined changes. The clustered interval for the boundary-F1 difference includes zero.

title: Published the complete six-state USBF update
summary: Published 25,092,517 buildings for Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Colorado and Connecticut, including 913,169 with recorded geometry changes. The complete new regional output replaced the older six-state records.
note: The other 42 states and DC retained their existing data. Publication completeness does not establish that every geometry change improves accuracy.
details: The release was organized as state-level GeoParquet shards at this date. Heights retain their source meaning; the footprint-refinement workflow does not estimate new building heights.

title: Added real data sources to the US Buildings website
summary: Added a data catalog, URL and local GeoJSON inputs, layer visibility and opacity controls, and feature inspection. The first connected sources included VIDA building data and USGS imagery.
note: The VIDA product combines Google, Microsoft and OpenStreetMap sources; its source labels are not three independent building inventories.

title: Completed and audited the six-state V7 footprint product
summary: Production and full source-identity coverage checks completed for Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Colorado and Connecticut: 25,092,517 buildings, including 913,169 with footprint modifications (about 3.64%).
note: This is a production-completeness result, not a new geometry-accuracy evaluation or a claim that the complete package has been uploaded. The frozen production model and scientific rules were unchanged.
details: Of 25,092,558 unique source IDs, all valid sources were accounted for with zero missing valid IDs and zero extra IDs. The remaining 41 records are verified invalid original geometries and remain explicitly quarantined. Counts by state: AL 2,846,169; AR 1,759,917; AZ 3,071,363; CA 13,243,143; CO 2,564,259; CT 1,607,666. Completion was recorded at 04:25 EDT on October 22.

title: Resumed regional production beyond the completed six states
summary: A separate regional generation continued toward the contiguous United States and DC, reusing completed six-state results. The October 22, 14:38 EDT snapshot recorded 31,814 additional buildings and 2,146 modifications around the Delaware–Maryland area.
note: These are dated progress counts, not a live monitor or a completed regional or national release. The current region still had 9,112 buildings outstanding at that snapshot.
details: The workflow retains complete input context across administrative boundaries, deduplicates shared grids, and separates processing context from delivery geography. Production and export/upload run independently; checkpoint continuation was scheduled, but scheduling alone does not establish successful continuation.

title: Defined complete regional replacement for incremental releases
summary: An accepted region will replace all older current-product records in that region with its complete new output, including unchanged buildings. Older data outside the accepted region remains in the current product.
note: The October 22 handoff recorded the complete six-state package in export and verification preparation; successful public upload of that package was not yet verified. The public repository link is not proof of this new release.

sources.label: Public data repository (check its current manifest)

details: Different old/new building counts are allowed. Region membership follows fixed original ownership, and whole footprints are retained. Missing inputs or failed work cannot be treated as an accepted empty region. The first replacement covers the six completed states; the other 42 states plus DC retain their existing data.

title: Completed a matched image-line refinement and DL comparison
summary: Compared an adaptation of Jung & Sohn (2019) with the existing DL-assisted local roof reassignment on eight Georgetown buildings under two shared-input settings. All 16 pairs share observations, footprints and the same initial Roofer model; the paper adaptation ran 48 optimization trials across three seeds.
note: This implements the paper’s core ideas with declared substitutions, not the original algorithm in full. Independent target roof ground truth is absent, so no real-world accuracy winner is established.
details: The adaptation uses NAIP line/corner cues, contour proposals, fitting and complexity terms, and annealed search while holding roof planes fixed. Twelve analytic cases showed aggregate improvement for boundary shifts but inconsistent orientation/corner behavior. Clean-package replay exactly reproduced one changed candidate from each method. Unchanged models and rejected candidates remain visible.

title: Tested local bumps, depressions and roof-plane reassignment
summary: A bounded validation reused frozen point-model scores on eight real buildings and tested 48 analytic cases. Two real local-replacement candidates were proposed; only one passed the fixed shell-edge diagnostic.
note: This is not a newly trained correction network. OSM 67521425 remains unresolved: its proposed changed candidate failed the edge check, and the checked export retains the preceding model. Geometric validity does not establish roof accuracy.

sources.label: Local repair methods, cases and models

details: The final validation preserves original XYZ and point indices and labels reassigned surfaces as generated geometry. Coherent planar contamination and total occlusion remain unresolved; low support alone does not justify flattening or filling a roof. Earlier invalid development probes were superseded by the corrected final run.

title: Compared fusion order and guarded canopy filtering
summary: Compared the original joint filtering workflow, point-cloud-first reconstruction, and strong point evidence with observed-plane protection on the same eight buildings. In two inspected cases, the guarded method removed 150 and 16 candidate points, compared with 10 and 6 in the original workflow.
note: Removed-point counts are not tree-classification accuracy. Lower model peaks do not prove a more accurate roof; both remaining canopy and mistakenly removed roof support require independent checks.

sources.label: Three methods, point decisions and roof models

details: The original fusion rule screened out only 136 of 21,383 candidates. Most suspected residual canopy points never reached the fusion threshold. The revised method allows strong point evidence to act despite optical conflict and protects points near supported planes. No new network was trained for this comparison.

title: Connected real inputs to an eight-building LoD2 workflow
summary: Connected NAIP imagery, original 3DEP points and footprints through conservative point filtering, Roofer reconstruction, semantic roof-support review, shell diagnostics and export. All eight cases produced native LoD2 outputs.
note: The first version removed 136 points at the front end but triggered no additional backend trimming. Initial and final models were therefore identical; this verifies execution, not backend effectiveness or improved accuracy.
details: Six roof surfaces with insufficient observed support were retained for review. Fully occluded roof completion is not implemented. The experiment keeps original point decisions, input provenance, failures and fallback records.

title: Expanded training and evaluated roof-support filtering across cities
summary: Completed 26 training runs across 16 configurations, with up to 20,000 training buildings. Evaluation covered 200 buildings in Groningen and Maastricht, 12 simulated observation conditions and 19 reconstruction workflows.
note: These results use automatic 3DBAG teacher roofs and simulated point observations. They do not establish accuracy on real AHN/3DEP data or US roofs. RGB imagery is for inspection, not an input to the newly trained point models.

sources.label: Controlled results and full experiment archive

details: The source-validation-selected local model reduced the mean penalized roof loss from 1.0940 to 0.5123 m. The loss includes failure and missing-coverage penalties; it is not successful-roof MAE. Extra gains from larger training sets and longer training were not clearly established. Real-point diagnostics still showed the risk of removing roof-support points.

title: Tested learned filtering and its clean-roof tradeoff
summary: A first cross-city study used 500 training, 160 validation and 160 test buildings from 3DBAG. A fixed 24-building subset underwent 720 roof reconstruction comparisons. Learned filtering reduced dense simulated canopy error but also damaged clean roofs.
note: The controlled experiments use simulated observations. A separate Boston probe on 18 real buildings and 47,544 candidates did not establish a reconstruction-success improvement or independently verified roof accuracy.
details: For dense simulated canopy, mean vertical error was 2.14 m for raw points, 1.27 m after PointNet filtering and 1.49 m with a local model plus roof protection. On clean roofs the corresponding values were 0.40, 0.55 and 0.52 m. Point-classification quality alone did not determine reconstruction quality.

title: Expanded the input-quality comparison to 120 buildings
summary: Extended the Georgetown comparison to the original 60 buildings plus 60 additional cases, testing 12 configurations. Local registration and aggressive simplification did not provide consistent benefits across the two groups.
note: Metrics use held-out observations from the same point-cloud acquisition, not independent roof ground truth. Improvements on the original cases did not consistently transfer to the additional cases.
details: Published the initial three experiment chapters together with actual model geometry, candidate/held-out point membership, imagery and per-building inspection. The current archive preserves those historical results.

title: Separated registration and point filtering in a four-way comparison
summary: Compared raw input, registration alone, point filtering alone and their combination on 60 fixed buildings. Combined preprocessing changed common-point mean absolute error from 0.6546 to 0.6513 m, while coverage fell from 99.69% to 93.83%.
note: The small common-point error reduction does not establish an overall quality gain. These are same-acquisition held-out observations, and the registration groups each included a candidate that failed the fixed edge diagnostic.
details: The global footprint translation was 0.25 m west and 1.00 m north; filtering removed 3.65% of candidate points. NAIP did not participate in this preprocessing reconstruction experiment. Original crop membership was fixed, so recovering newly available points after registration remained untested.

title: Established five reconstruction baselines in Georgetown
summary: Built a 60-building pilot using 2014 NAIP imagery, 2014 3DEP points and USBF footprints. Compared native Roofer, LiDAR roof templates, image-oriented templates, free-plane reconstruction and image-assisted plane partitioning.
note: The best held-out fit in this pilot was Roofer at 0.743 m MAE. Evaluation used a fixed 20% holdout from the same LiDAR acquisition, not independent ground truth. No new deep-learning model was trained in this round.
details: Simple optical orientation cues provided limited gains, and none of the tested alternatives surpassed Roofer on this metric. This motivated closer inspection of registration, contamination, roof support and topology.

title: Audited reference data before treating city models as roof truth
summary: Reviewed the distinction between footprint-and-height extrusion and roof-structure reconstruction, and audited potential LoD2 reference sources. The research direction narrowed toward using real observations to adapt roof reconstruction across regions.
note: Automatically reconstructed city models and building-energy models are not automatically independent roof ground truth. Pairing, acquisition time, registration, roof detail and fallback geometry need to be checked separately.
details: The planned evaluation separates point support, plane/ridge structure, coverage, reconstruction failure and shell validity. These are research requirements, not evidence that the proposed method is already accurate.

title: Rebased manuscript review on the author-reviewed draft
summary: The manuscript discussion identified the author-reviewed USBF draft as the baseline for further sentence-level review and emphasized describing specific footprint-editing scenarios rather than broadly claiming improved accuracy.
note: This records a manuscript-review decision, not submission, acceptance or confirmation that every suggested edit was incorporated. Selected visual changes do not override aggregate evaluation results.

title: Reviewed the current footprint production and recovery checkpoint
summary: The latest project handoff recorded substantial progress in the building-footprint production workflow and a completed producer segment that committed new buildings. Work to recover storage capacity and resume the next production segment was still in progress.
note: This describes the October 16 project snapshot, not a verified live status or a completed nationwide release. A proposed million-file recovery target had not been certified.

title: Verified new buildings from a regional production run
summary: A bounded regional run ended cleanly, reporting 14,876 newly committed buildings and 779 footprint modifications. A separate trial showed that a larger input catalog could produce and verify another nonempty building batch.
note: These are regional and trial results, not a nationwide completion count. A two-host computing pilot remained separate from the canonical production workflow.

title: Tested an indexed input archive for footprint processing
summary: Independent component checks and bounded real-data comparisons showed that archived inputs could be read while preserving the tested building geometry and output attributes.
note: These checks did not establish nationwide throughput or authorize removal of the original inputs.

title: Prepared a highlighted manuscript and sentence-level review
summary: Prepared a highlighted revision of the manuscript and supplementary methods, checked citation numbering, and created a separate sentence-level review with optional tracked English suggestions.
note: The suggested edits are separate from the highlighted revision. Structural checks passed, but desktop Word rendering and independent validation of footprint changes were not completed.

title: Completed a guarded footprint-input cleanup batch
summary: A verified cleanup batch removed eligible intermediate pixel files after checking product identities, input dependencies and recoverability. The work freed storage capacity for continued footprint production.
note: The remaining storage constraint was not resolved by this batch, and the removed files were a bounded eligible cohort rather than the full input collection.

title: Prepared tracked revisions to the manuscript and methods
summary: Prepared Word tracked-change versions of the main manuscript and supplementary methods. The revision clarified the distinction between national counts and regional evaluation, refined method descriptions, and updated figures and cross-references.
note: The shared source manuscript was not overwritten. Independent evidence that every modified footprint improved remains an open research question; this entry does not indicate submission or acceptance.

title: Compared footprint pipeline revisions on matched inputs
summary: Repeated isolated comparisons found matching building attributes, geometry, ownership and candidate records between the existing and revised workflows. The revision reduced elapsed time in these tests, but missed its planned speedup targets.
note: The measured gains came from isolated test cohorts. Sustained improvement in live production had not been established.

title: Completed controlled NAIP footprint-model training studies
summary: Across October 2-4, several matched training comparisons explored model structure, quality retention and residual learning for aerial-image building footprints. The inspected run logs show the training and validation stages completed.
note: The inspected logs do not establish which candidate improved held-out footprint accuracy.

title: Verified a single-building energy-model run
summary: An AutoBEM/OpenStudio example generated a building model, simulation inputs and time-series electricity output, and its run report marked the example successful.
note: This verifies one building example; batch modeling and validation against observed energy use remain to be demonstrated.

title: Revised the manuscript's building-product section
